encounters.cc: recurrent urinary tract infections, dysuria, and a sensation of incomplete bladder emptying

lines: Recurrent urinary tract infections, dysuria, and a sensation of incomplete bladder emptying
A 32-year-old woman presents to the clinic with a 6-month history of recurrent urinary tract infections, dysuria, and a sensation of incomplete bladder emptying.
She also reports occasional postvoid dribbling and dyspareunia.
Her past medical history is significant for childbirth 2 years ago with a second-degree perineal tear.
- Prenatal vitamin with iron 1 tablet daily
- Nitrofurantoin 100 mg nightly for UTI prophylaxis
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: No alcohol use. Occupation: Elementary school teacher.
On physical examination, a tender anterior vaginal wall mass is palpated, which expresses purulent discharge when pressure is applied

encounters.cc: presents to the obstetrics clinic for a routine prenatal visit

lines: She presents to the obstetrics clinic for a routine prenatal visit
The patient returns for routine prenatal care with uterine leiomyomas, urethral diverticulum, and gestational hypertension.
She reports feeling well with no complaints of contractions, vaginal bleeding, or leakage of fluid, and her pregnancy has been uncomplicated with regular prenatal care.
Her first pregnancy resulted in a normal vaginal delivery of a healthy infant.
- Prenatal vitamin with iron 1 tablet daily
- Nitrofurantoin 100 mg nightly for UTI prophylaxis
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: No alcohol use. Occupation: Elementary school teacher.
On examination, her vital signs are within normal limits
The fundal height measurement is noted to be greater than expected for gestational age.
An ultrasound is performed, which reveals an amniotic fluid index (AFI) of 26 cm with no fetal anomalies or evidence of gastrointestinal obstruction.
The fetus is in a cephalic presentation with normal growth parameters.

encounters.cc: presents to the obstetrics clinic for a routine prenatal visit

lines: She presents to the obstetrics clinic for a routine prenatal visit
Patient returns for prenatal care with leiomyomas and diverticulum and reports feeling well with good fetal movement.
Her first pregnancy was uncomplicated, and she had a vaginal delivery at term.
- Prenatal vitamin with iron 1 tablet daily
- Nitrofurantoin 100 mg nightly for UTI prophylaxis
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: No alcohol use. Occupation: Elementary school teacher.
Her blood pressure is 120/78 mmHg, heart rate is 82 beats per minute
On examination, fundal height is consistent with gestational age.
An ultrasound is performed, which shows the fetus in a transverse lie with the spine perpendicular to the mother's long axis.
There are no other abnormalities noted on the ultrasound.

encounters.cc: presents to the obstetrics clinic for a routine prenatal visit

lines: She presents to the obstetrics clinic for a routine prenatal visit
She returns for prenatal care at 36 weeks with diverticulum and transverse lie.
She reports feeling well but notes fetal movements differ from first pregnancy.
Her past medical history is significant for uterine leiomyomas diagnosed two years ago, which have been asymptomatic and monitored with serial ultrasounds.
Her first child was delivered vaginally at term without complications.
- Prenatal vitamin with iron 1 tablet daily
- Nitrofurantoin 100 mg nightly for UTI prophylaxis
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: No alcohol use. Occupation: Elementary school teacher.
On examination, the fundal height is appropriate for gestational age, and fetal heart tones are normal.
An ultrasound is performed, which shows the fetus in a breech position with the buttocks presenting closest to the cervix.
The ultrasound also confirms the presence of multiple leiomyomas, the largest of which is located at the fundus of the uterus.

encounters.cc: presents to the labor and delivery unit with regular contractions every 5 minutes for the past 2 hours

lines: She presents to the labor and delivery unit with regular contractions every 5 minutes for the past 2 hours

Returning to the labor and delivery unit with regular contractions every 5 minutes, the patient has histories of uterine leiomyomas, urethral diverticulum, and gestational hypertension, and was evaluated earlier this pregnancy for recurrent urinary symptoms, polyhydramnios, and fetal malpresentation.
Her prenatal course was unremarkable, and she desires a vaginal delivery.
She reports that her previous delivery was via cesarean section due to breech presentation.
On further questioning, she reveals that the cesarean was performed through a vertical incision on the upper uterus because the baby was in an awkward position.
- Prenatal vitamin with iron 1 tablet daily
- Nitrofurantoin 100 mg nightly for UTI prophylaxis
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: No alcohol use. Occupation: Elementary school teacher.
On examination, her vital signs are stable
The cervix is dilated to 4 cm, and the fetus is in a cephalic presentation.

encounters.cc: presents to the obstetrics clinic for a routine prenatal visit.

lines: She presents to the obstetrics clinic for a routine prenatal visit.
Patient with uterine leiomyomas and prior cesarean returns for prenatal care.
Her current pregnancy has been unremarkable until now.
She reports occasional shortness of breath but denies vaginal bleeding, leakage of fluid, or contractions.
Her first pregnancy was uncomplicated, and she had a spontaneous vaginal delivery at term.
- Prenatal vitamin with iron 1 tablet daily
- Nitrofurantoin 100 mg nightly for UTI prophylaxis
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: No alcohol use. Occupation: Elementary school teacher.
On examination, her blood pressure is 120/78 mmHg, heart rate is 88 beats per minute, and fetal heart rate is 140 beats per minute.
The obstetric examination reveals a fundal height consistent with gestational age, but the fetal position is suspected to be breech on palpation.
Her prenatal labs have been normal, including a negative gestational diabetes screen.
An ultrasound confirms a breech presentation with the fetus in a frank breech position.
Additionally, the ultrasound shows placenta previa with the placenta covering the internal cervical os.

encounters.cc: severe right upper quadrant pain, nausea, and vomiting

lines: Severe right upper quadrant pain, nausea, and vomiting

This 37-year-old female with uterine leiomyomas, urethral diverticulum on UTI prophylaxis, and placenta previa with hemorrhage presents to the emergency department with a 24-hour history of severe right upper quadrant pain, nausea, and vomiting.
She reports the pain is constant and radiates to her back.
She has a history of gestational hypertension in her previous pregnancy.
- Prenatal vitamin with iron 1 tablet daily
- Nitrofurantoin 100 mg nightly for UTI prophylaxis
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: No alcohol use. Occupation: Elementary school teacher.
Her blood pressure is 160/100 mmHg, and her pulse is 98 beats per minute.
Physical examination reveals right upper quadrant tenderness without rebound or guarding.
Reflexes are brisk, and there is no ankle edema.
The fetal heart tracing is reactive without decelerations.

encounters.cc: presents to the emergency department with a 2-day history of persistent nausea, vomiting, and right upper quadrant pain

lines: She presents to the emergency department with a 2-day history of persistent nausea, vomiting, and right upper quadrant pain
The patient with uterine leiomyomas, urethral diverticulum, and prior severe preeclampsia returns with similar complaints.
She reports that her pain is constant and radiates to her back.
She denies any history of gallstones or alcohol use.
Her pregnancy has been uncomplicated until now.
- Prenatal vitamin with iron 1 tablet daily
- Nitrofurantoin 100 mg nightly for UTI prophylaxis
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: No alcohol use. Occupation: Elementary school teacher.
On examination, her blood pressure is 135/85 mmHg, heart rate is 102 beats per minute, and she is afebrile.
Her skin and sclera are anicteric.
Abdominal examination reveals tenderness in the right upper quadrant without rebound or guarding.
Urinalysis is normal. There is no proteinuria.
